system:
You write one step of a hands-on tutorial from the evidence of a demonstration video: the narration spoken during the step, text descriptions of the hands (from hand landmarks; may be wrong when hands are occluded), and a few frames from inside the step (attached images, in time order). The reader is a learner who will repeat the procedure without the video.

Write:
- title: a short imperative title (max ~8 words).
- instruction: one or two imperative sentences saying exactly what to do.
- details: extra how-to points that are actually supported by the evidence (hand position, grip,
  order of sub-actions). Empty if none.
- tools and materials: only those named in the narration or clearly visible in the frames, as short
  labels (1-3 words, e.g. "soap", "paper towel").
- expected_result: what the learner should see when the step is done, or null if not evident.
- cautions: only cautions stated in the narration or obvious from what is shown (e.g. a blade).
- confidence: 0-1, how well the evidence supports your description.
- missing_info: everything a learner would need but the evidence does not state.
- substeps: the step's action phases for the tutorial video, 1 to 4, in time order. Split
  only where the action visibly or audibly changes (e.g. "scrub palms" then "scrub between fingers");
  one phase is fine for a single action. For each phase:
  - start_s: one of the listed anchor times (the first phase starts at the step start).
  - caption: on-screen text, imperative, at most 44 characters (about 6 words).
  - focus_box: the id of the listed focus box that best shows this phase (e.g. the work zone while the
    hands manipulate something, both hands for whole-hand actions), or "full" when the surroundings
    matter (e.g. reaching for a tap or a door). Only use listed ids; never invent coordinates.
  - emphasis: optional 1-3 word callout of the exact spot a learner should watch (e.g. "between
    fingers", "under nails"), at most 24 characters, only if the narration or the frames
    show it; else null. emphasis_s: when it applies (inside the phase), else null.

Grounding rules (strict):
- Never invent numeric values: quantities, durations, counts, temperatures, speeds, settings,
  concentrations, sizes. If the narration does not state a number, do not write one; add a
  missing_info item (field quantity / duration / setting) instead. This applies to captions too.
- Never invent tool or material names you cannot see or hear; use a generic description and add a
  missing_info item (field tool / material) if the specific item matters.
- Never invent safety or compliance claims. If the action looks hazardous and no precaution is stated,
  add a missing_info item with field safety.
- Mark a missing_info item blocking when a learner could not perform the step correctly or safely
  without it.
- The previous/next step summaries are context only; describe this step alone.
user:
Step 21 of 22, 592.5s to 649.9s.
Segmentation summary: Explain the nozzle scrubbing mechanical update and how the nozzle sweeps across the wiper.
Previous step: Point out the wiper nubs to emphasize the importance of precise alignment.
Next step: Use the printer's touchscreen console to home the axes and enter G-code commands to test nozzle positioning.

Narration during this step:
[594.7-598.4s] "the amount that you run the wiper, you really don't need to get that"
[598.4-603.3s] "aggressive with the scrubbing. The scrubbing was only really necessary on the"
[603.3-607.9s] "earlier releases because we didn't have the AMS stuff set up yet. So we were"
[607.9-612.6s] "just running the scrub on the start-up routine and then it wouldn't scrub"
[612.6-617.4s] "again until the next print. So we were taking you know full advantage of having"
[617.4-624.0s] "that wiper there to get the most scrubbing possible. So now all we're doing in"
[624.0-630.2s] "this recent update is we're just sweeping on the X and then we're step on the"
[630.2-635.0s] "end of on the end of the wiper. We're step up and then we'll sweep on the X"
[635.0-638.2s] "again and then we'll step down and we'll sweep on the X again and that's the"
[638.2-646.6s] "wiper team. So now it's not overly critical for the X positioning but it is"
[646.6-651.1s] "critical on the Y positioning but not as critical as it would have been on the X."

response.title: Understand the Nozzle Wiper Update
response.instruction: Observe the improved nozzle scrubbing movement. The updated wiper routine now performs a three-stage sweep across the nozzle.
details: The updated wiper sequence moves the nozzle in three passes along the X-axis, stepping up or down between each horizontal sweep.
Precise Y-axis positioning is critical, while X-axis positioning is now less critical than in previous versions.

missing_info.description: The specific firmware version or software update this change refers to is not named.
